memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Cursed is anyone who dishonours their father or mother.' ... 'Cursed is anyone who moves their neighbour's boundary stone.' ... 'Cursed is anyone who leads the blind astray on the road.' ... 'Cursed is anyone who withholds justice from the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow.' Then all the people shall say, 'Amen!'" — Deut 27:16-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These curses move through everyday relationships — how we treat our parents, our neighbours, the vulnerable, and the weak. Dishonouring father and mother, secretly stealing a neighbour's land by moving a boundary stone, misleading a blind person who cannot see the danger, denying justice to the foreigner, orphan, and widow. Each one exposes a way we can quietly harm others when we think no one will hold us accountable.

Do you see the thread running through them? They are all sins against people who cannot easily defend themselves. The blind cannot see the trap. The orphan has no parent to protect them. The widow has no husband to plead her case. God takes special notice of how we treat those who have no power to fight back.

This tells us something wonderful about God's character. He is the defender of the defenceless. He sees the hidden cruelty the world overlooks, and He cares deeply about justice for the weak. The way we treat the vulnerable reveals the true condition of our hearts.

Jesus lived this out perfectly, welcoming the overlooked and defending the weak, and He calls us to reflect His heart (Jas 1:27). So honour your parents. Deal honestly. Protect the vulnerable. In doing so, you show the character of the God who defends them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do I treat those who cannot repay or defend themselves?
2. Am I honest in the hidden dealings no one else sees?
3. Who among the vulnerable is God calling me to protect and honour?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You defend the weak and the overlooked. Give me Your heart for the vulnerable, honesty in my dealings, and honour for those I am called to respect. Amen.
